summary: Antoine Cabaton worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the École du Louvre and the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1895–1898), and held a post at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (~1895).
Antoine Lutz completed his PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University under the doctoral supervision of Francisco J. Varela.

Antoine Meillet was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Paris, Sorbonne, and EPHE under Saussure, Darmesteter, and Lévi, later holding posts at EPHE, INALCO, and the Collège de France (1905–1936).

Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy was a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. He held professorships at INALCO and the Collège de France (1806–1838), and served as president of the Société Asiatique and perpetual secretary of the AIBL.
Antoine-Louis Henri de Polier was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He studied under the traditional teacher Ramchandra and served as a Colonel in the East India Company.

Antoine-Léonard Chézy worked in Indology and linguistics, studying under Louis-Mathieu Langlès and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held positions at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, taught Persian at INALCO, and held the Sanskrit chair at the Collège de France (1815–1832).

Anton Boller was an Indologist and linguist who became a corresponding member of the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 1848. He served at the University of Vienna as Dozent, extraordinary professor, and ordinary professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit from 1845.

Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his Dr. phil. at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1828–1831), later serving there as a Dozent (1849–1852) after a post at the Royal Danish Library (~1838–1840).

Anton Schiefner worked in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Saint Petersburg State University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences, the Russian Academy of Sciences library, and Saint Petersburg Roman Catholic Theological Academy.
Anton Westermann was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Leipzig from 1825 to 1830 and served there as co-director from 1830 to 1865.

Antonino Forte was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held professorships at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1976–2006), Hōbōgirin, and the Italian School of East Asian Studies, and directed the Kyoto Center of the Istituto Italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente.

Antonio T. de Nicolás worked in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Fordham University (~1968–1971) and served as professor emeritus of philosophy at Stony Brook University, where he held a post from ~1969 to 2000.

Antonio Terrone is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter and Barend J. ter Haar, and has served as scholar in residence at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

Anuj Misra is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied under Clemency Montelle and Kim Plofker and has served as an external researcher at the University of Copenhagen (attested 2026).

Anukul Chandra Banerjee worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya, earned his PhD at the University of Calcutta, where he was assistant lecturer in Pali (attested 1943), and directed the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1981).

Archibald Edward Gough worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under Monier Monier-Williams. He held professorships at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Presidency University, and served as principal of Aliah University (~1881–1895).
Arghyadip Mondal works in Buddhist studies, computational fields, and Indology. He has been a PhD researcher and faculty member at Ghent University (attested 2026).
Ariane Macdonald is a Tibetologist who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Arindam Chakrabarti is a philosopher and Indologist who earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford. He held professorships at the University of Delhi, the University of Hawaiʻi, and the Mattoo Endowed Chair at Stony Brook University.
Arinde L. Jonker works in the field of Indology. She completed a Research MA at Leiden University (attested 2018), where she studied with Jonathan A. Silk and was supervised by Peter C. Bisschop.
